verses.1: The message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan the chief executioner had sent him from Ramah, when he had captured him in chains among the captives from Jerusalem and Judah being taken to Babylon.
verses.2: Nebuzaradan took him and said to him: "The LORD your God has spoken this evil concerning this place.
verses.3: And the LORD has done it, because you sinned against the LORD and did not listen to his voice. Now this will happen to you."
verses.4: "Now look, I have set you free today from the chains on your hands. If it is good in your eyes, to come with me to Babylon, come. I will look after you. But if it is evil in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, then turn back. See, the whole land is open before you. Go wherever it seems right and good to you.
verses.5: Moreover, you must not turn back or return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah. Stay with him among the people, or go wherever it seems good and right to you." Then Nebuzaradan gave him provisions and a gift and sent him on his way.
verses.6: So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah at Mizpah and stayed among the people who had been left in the land.
verses.7: All the army commanders in the field—themselves and their men—heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan over the land, and that he had placed with him some men, women, and children who had not been taken to Babylon.
verses.8: So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah—Ismael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Jonathan son of Kareah, and Seraiyah son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Zephaniah son of Maacath.
verses.9: Gedaliah swore to them and to their men in the name of the LORD, saying, "Do not be afraid of serving the Chaldeans. Stay in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well for you.
verses.10: As for me, I will remain in Mizpah to stand in the presence of the Chaldeans who may come to us. But you, gather wine, oil, and summer produce and store them in your vessels, and remain in your towns where you have taken refuge."
verses.11: All the Jews in Moab, in the land of the Ammonites, in Edom, and in all the other lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan over them.
verses.12: So all the Jews from every place where they had been scattered came to Gedaliah at Mizpah in the land of Judah. They gathered together wine, summer produce, and oil in great quantity.
verses.13: Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders in the field came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
verses.14: They said to him, "Do you know that Baalis the king of the Ammonites has sent Ismael son of Nethaniah to kill you?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.
verses.15: Johanan son of Kareah spoke secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah, saying, "Let me please go and strike down Ismael son of Nethaniah. No one will know it. Why should he kill you and cause all the Jews who have gathered to you to be scattered and the remnant of Judah to be destroyed?"
verses.16: But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do this thing, for you are speaking falsely against Ismael."

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "chief executioner" (רַב־טַבָּחִים) is a literal translation of the title, which may also be interpreted as "chief of the eunuchs" or "chief of the palace officials," depending on context.
- v. 4: "to come with me to Babylon" is a direct translation of "לָבוֹא אִתִּי בָבֶל," though "to Babylon" is a noun phrase here.
- v. 9: "Chaldeans" is used consistently in the translation for clarity, though the Hebrew term is "כַּשְׂדִּים."
- v. 15: "Let me please go and strike down" is a natural rendering of the imperative form of the Hebrew verb "כַּהֲרָה" (to strike down).
raw:
[1] The message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan the chief executioner had sent him from Ramah, when he had captured him in chains among the captives from Jerusalem and Judah being taken to Babylon.

[2] Nebuzaradan took him and said to him: "The LORD your God has spoken this evil concerning this place.

[3] And the LORD has done it, because you sinned against the LORD and did not listen to his voice. Now this will happen to you."

[4] "Now look, I have set you free today from the chains on your hands. If it is good in your eyes, to come with me to Babylon, come. I will look after you. But if it is evil in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, then turn back. See, the whole land is open before you. Go wherever it seems right and good to you.

[5] Moreover, you must not turn back or return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah. Stay with him among the people, or go wherever it seems good and right to you." Then Nebuzaradan gave him provisions and a gift and sent him on his way.

[6] So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah at Mizpah and stayed among the people who had been left in the land.

[7] All the army commanders in the field—themselves and their men—heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan over the land, and that he had placed with him some men, women, and children who had not been taken to Babylon.

[8] So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah—Ismael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Jonathan son of Kareah, and Seraiyah son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Zephaniah son of Maacath.

[9] Gedaliah swore to them and to their men in the name of the LORD, saying, "Do not be afraid of serving the Chaldeans. Stay in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well for you.

[10] As for me, I will remain in Mizpah to stand in the presence of the Chaldeans who may come to us. But you, gather wine, oil, and summer produce and store them in your vessels, and remain in your towns where you have taken refuge."

[11] All the Jews in Moab, in the land of the Ammonites, in Edom, and in all the other lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan over them.

[12] So all the Jews from every place where they had been scattered came to Gedaliah at Mizpah in the land of Judah. They gathered together wine, summer produce, and oil in great quantity.

[13] Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders in the field came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.

[14] They said to him, "Do you know that Baalis the king of the Ammonites has sent Ismael son of Nethaniah to kill you?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

[15] Johanan son of Kareah spoke secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah, saying, "Let me please go and strike down Ismael son of Nethaniah. No one will know it. Why should he kill you and cause all the Jews who have gathered to you to be scattered and the remnant of Judah to be destroyed?"

[16] But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do this thing, for you are speaking falsely against Ismael."

- v. 1: "chief executioner" (רַב־טַבָּחִים) is a literal translation of the title, which may also be interpreted as "chief of the eunuchs" or "chief of the palace officials," depending on context.
- v. 4: "to come with me to Babylon" is a direct translation of "לָבוֹא אִתִּי בָבֶל," though "to Babylon" is a noun phrase here.
- v. 9: "Chaldeans" is used consistently in the translation for clarity, though the Hebrew term is "כַּשְׂדִּים."
- v. 15: "Let me please go and strike down" is a natural rendering of the imperative form of the Hebrew verb "כַּהֲרָה" (to strike down).
